Our Services

One-on-One Developmental Therapy

Individualized, child-centered sessions that build on each child’s unique strengths and needs. We support development, learning, communication, social-emotional skills, independence, and participation in family and community routines.

Group Sessions

Interactive group activities that foster social and cognitive growth.

Parent Coaching

We work with families to create meaningful goals, reinforce learning at home, and build lasting progress. Your child’s success is our success.

Who We Serve

Infants and toddlers ages 0–3, including children with developmental delays and disabilities, neurodiversity, behavior challenges, physical disabilities, and medically fragile or complex needs. Every child has potential. We’re here to help them thrive.

Our Approach

  • Play-Based Learning: Children learn best through play. Our sessions build foundational developmental and early academic skills.
  • Whole Child Focus: We consider the whole child, how development affects the family unit, and how families can understand and nurture their child’s growth.
  • Small, Meaningful Steps: Building skills for long-term success.
  • Flexible Service Delivery: Home, daycare, park, community settings, or mutually agreed locations.
  • Family Collaboration: Together, we create meaningful goals and lasting progress.

Our Mission

Nurturing Developing Minds supports the growth and development of infants and toddlers by addressing the whole child and empowering families to actively participate in their child’s developmental journey.

Location: Flossmoor, IL

Goals & Outcomes

Our work is guided by four goals:

  • Serve infants and toddlers with developmental delays and disabilities.
  • Improve developmental milestones in communication, behavior, social skills, and motor skills.
  • Increase parent and caregiver confidence in supporting their child’s development.
  • Reduce delays in accessing early intervention services.

Meet Stacey

Stacey Richardson-Ellis, Owner and Director

Stacey brings 28 years of experience as a developmental therapist, a degree in Early Childhood Education, and certifications in infant mental health and play-based therapy.

Stacey brings unparalleled expertise to every child’s journey.

Professional Experience

  • Northwestern University — Reduce the Wait (RTW) Project: Participated in a research project focused on reducing wait times for autism diagnosis. Stacey completed extensive training and worked alongside a speech pathologist and a developmental pediatrician on a medical diagnostic team evaluating children for autism.
  • Rush University Medical Center — RISE Project: Participated in research through the Reciprocal Imitation and Social Engagement (RISE) Project, coaching parents of children with delays in social communication. Her work included certification in an evidence-based parent-coaching intervention, Reciprocal Imitation Teaching (RIT).
  • Direct Developmental Therapy: Extensive experience supporting infants and toddlers with developmental delays, including neurodiverse and medically complex children.

As a mother of three, Stacey brings both professional expertise and personal understanding to supporting families through early developmental challenges.

Expanding Access to Care

We are seeking funding to expand access to high-quality developmental therapy for infants and toddlers with developmental delays, including children who are medically fragile and neurodiverse.

Funding will support therapy services, developmental and learning materials, and outreach to underserved families, helping more children and caregivers access the support they need.

To discuss funding or supporting our program, contact us by email.
